reasoning_traces.think:
The TimesFM architecture defines a foundational mapping from time-series segments to forecasts using a decoder-only transformer. It operates by breaking input sequences into overlapping patches of fixed size (p=32), which are then processed through an MLP-based residual block and positional encoding before entering a stacked causal transformer. Each output token is generated sequentially based on previous tokens, producing a forecast for the next patch length (h=128). The model uses random patch masking during training to simulate varying context lengths up to 512 points. This structure enables zero-shot forecasting across diverse domains but lacks probabilistic outputs and covariate support. In GSI, this framework supports Bayesian inference by treating each patch as evidence for posterior updates. In GSE, it enables state transitions through temporal reasoning over game sequences, though requires extension for uncertainty quantification and domain-specific inputs.
